label: UniFi Dream Router
description: UniFi Dream Router (UDR) - 4x 1G RJ45 LAN (2 PoE, 802.3af) plus 1x 1G RJ45 WAN, the four LAN sockets on one 802.1Q bridge. WiFi 6; 40 W PoE budget; 19.37 W max.

poe.note: 40 W from the vendor datasheet, which prints it as its own row: "PoE budget 40W" beside "PoE interface (2) PoE (Pair B 4, 5+; 7, 8-)" and "Max. PoE wattage per port by PSE 15.4W" - two of the five GbE ports source 802.3af, so at most 30.8 W of the 40 W can be drawn and the budget never binds. The tech-spec table carries the same three figures (PoE Budget 40W / PoE 15.4W / Voltage Range PoE Mode 44-57V): https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udr (read 2026-11-19). Before this, the row declared poe-pse and two poeOut ports with no budget at all, and the PoE allocator skips a PSE whose budget is 0 - so the Dream Router could not power a single phone. Per-socket ceiling, measured 2026-11-21: the two PSE sockets carried the bare direction bit `poeOut: true`, which `Device.poeDraw()` (engine/device.js) adds into the watt total as **1 W** - two 15.4 W access points on eth0/eth1 made `poeDraw()` answer 2 W and the 40 W budget could never be spent. The vendor prints the ceiling beside the budget: "Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE PoE = 15.4W" with "PoE Budget = 40W" and the census "1 GbE RJ45 = 5 (2 PoE)" (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udr, HTTP 200, 685,837 B, server-rendered spec table, read 2026-11-21; the datasheet row "Max. PoE wattage per port by PSE 15.4W" is the same figure). eth0 and eth1 now declare 15.4 W each; the class word `PoE` and the two-of-five census are unchanged.

notes:
Power: none of these copper ports accepts PoE. Vendor page https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udr (HTTP 200, 685,837 B, read 2026-11-19, server-rendered tech-spec table) says "Power Method = Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 1.1A Max, 50/60 Hz (the datasheet https://dl.ui.com/ds/udr_ds.pdf, 200, 771,202 B, says the same)"; a box fed from mains, a USB-C supply or a DC jack has no PoE-PD front end, so eth2 / eth3 / eth4 now declare poeIn: false. Without that declaration the engine's isPoePd() match on "unifi" gave each silent copper port a 12.95 W 802.3af draw - the defect PR #2118 and PR #2121 fixed across the UXG family (refs #130).

WiFi: the Dream Router carries an 802.11ax (WiFi 6) access point - "MIMO 2.4 GHz 4 x 4 / 5 GHz 4 x 4", "Throughput rate 2.4 GHz 600 Mbps / 5 GHz 2.4 Gbps", "WiFi standards 802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax" in its own datasheet https://dl.ui.com/ds/udr_ds.pdf (HTTP 200, 771,202 B, 3 pages, text layer) and the same rows on https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udr (HTTP 200, 685,837 B, read 2026-11-19). Hence radio0 = 2.4 GHz at 600 Mbps and radio1 = 5 GHz at 2.4 Gbps, both 4x4. `bands` is declared per radio because engine/media.js would otherwise give the 2.4 Gbps radio the whole 802.11ax band set, 6 GHz included, which this chassis does not have.

LAN bank is a bridge, not four routed ports (read 2026-11-21). Ubiquiti's own device fingerprint lists the UDR's `deviceCapabilities` as GATEWAY, **SWITCH**, ACCESS_POINT, NETWORK_APPLICATION, PROTECT_APPLICATION, CONTROLLER, APPLICATION_MODE, HAS_CLIENTS (sku UDR, sysid eccc) at https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, read 2026-11-21) - so the vendor classes this console as a switch, not only a gateway. The tech-spec table quantifies it: `MAC Address Table Size = 1,000` and `VLAN/Subnet-based Traffic Segmentation = True`, beside `Port Layout 1 GbE RJ45 = 5 (2 PoE) (1G/100M/10M)` at https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udr (HTTP 200, 685,837 B, read 2026-11-21), and the datasheet prints `VLAN 802.1Q` in its Software block at https://dl.ui.com/ds/udr_ds.pdf (HTTP 200, 771,202 B, 3 pp). A 1,000-entry MAC table is a bridge forwarding database and 802.1Q tagging is a switch feature, so the four LAN sockets forward at layer 2 and the row declares `l2-forward` (MAC learning + flooding only; VLAN and STP ride on it). Before this, `switchport access vlan 10` answered "cannot switch frames: it has no l2-forward capability" and two hosts on eth0 and eth1 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP.

WAN role and the 1G speed caps, same two surfaces. The datasheet splits the chassis as `Networking interface LAN: (4) GbE RJ45 ports / WAN: (1) GbE RJ45 port` (771,202 B PDF above), and the fingerprint's port diagram for the same SKU is `01 02 03 04 __ 05` - four sockets grouped, a fifth set apart, the same 4+1 pattern the fingerprint gives UDM (`01 02 03 04 __ 05`) and UCG-Ultra, both of which Ubiquiti documents as four LAN plus one WAN. eth4 is therefore the separated fifth socket and now carries `role: "wan"`, so `ip nat outside` can be cabled to the uplink; the four LAN ports stay switchable and `no switchport` still makes any of them routed. `speedCaps` gained 10M because the tech-spec Port Layout row prints the trio (1G/100M/10M); the earlier row stopped at 100M and a 10M-only sensor could not negotiate.

WAN/LAN separation, from the rows above (measured 2026-11-21). The datasheet splits the chassis as `Networking interface LAN: (4) GbE RJ45 ports / WAN: (1) GbE RJ45 port` (https://dl.ui.com/ds/udr_ds.pdf, HTTP 200, 771,202 B, 3 pp, text layer read 2026-11-21), and the tech-spec table repeats it as `Default WAN Ports (1) GbE RJ45`, `Max. WAN Port Count 1` (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udr, HTTP 200, 685,837 B, read 2026-11-21). eth4 is the WAN socket, but the four LAN sockets declared no `role`, and the engine's separation check (engine/device.js `ownsIpOn`, "WAN and LAN are separate L3 surfaces") needs a role on both sides to fire - so `ownsIpOn(eth4, '192.168.1.1')` returned true with 192.168.1.1/24 on eth0, and a host cabled to eth4 in that subnet got an ICMP reply from the LAN gateway. The four LAN ports now declare `role: "lan"`. Measured after the change: the WAN socket no longer owns the LAN address, a host on eth1 still reaches the address held on eth0, an address on eth4 is still answered on eth4, and the radios stay role-less - a wireless client is still answered by the same bridge, which is what the UDR's access point is for. Gate: test/ubiquiti-wan-lan-role-separation.test.js.
